Mr. Mesbahul Islam (Asif), Advocate ------ For the Petitioners
None appears ------ For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Mahmud Hossain (Nanmin) and others
Vs.
Hachen Matubbor and others
full_judgment:
F.R.M. Nazmul Ahasan, J: This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 29.04.2012 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Madaripur in Title Appeal No. 36 of 2008 reversing those dated 21.07.2008 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Madaripur Sadar, Madaripur in Title Suit No. 40 of 2005 decreeing the suit should not be set-aside.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration of title along with further declaration that the order dated 28.02.1974 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. XIII-3137/M-1005/1972-73 and the order dated 06.01.2006 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. XIII-B-14/2003-04 by the office of the defendant No. 15 are illegal and inoperative with further declaration that the Mutation Case No. IX-P-I-254, M.P.R/2001- 02 of the plaintiffs is still in force as well as another declaration that the deed dated 03.04.1974 being No. 2679 of the defendant No. 1 is forged, inoperative and void.

3. The plaintiff's case; in short, is that the scheduled land to the plaint belonged to the tenant A. Wahed Howlader who proposed to sell out the suit land with an agreement to re-convey the same. The predecessor of the plaintiffs, A. Aziz Mollah agreed to purchase the suit land. Accordingly, the suit land was sold out by a registered deed of sale dated 11.02.1965 being No. 673 with a registered deed of re-conveyance for a period of 7 years. The said period was expired on 11.02.1972 as A. Wahed Howlader did not take back the suit land by any registered deed repaying the consideration money for which the deed of sale dated 11.02.1965 being No. 673 became an out and out deed of sale. While enjoying the possession of the suit land, Aziz Mollah died leaving one son Shahjahan Mollah who died leaving the plaintiffs as his heirs. The plaintiffs have been enjoying the possession of the suit land by paying rents after getting their names mutated. The defendant No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case against the said mutation before the office of the defendant No. 15 stating for the first time about the result of the Miscellaneous Case No. XIII-3137/M-1005/1972-73 filed before the erstwhile C.O. (Revenue), Madaripur now Assistant Commissioner (Revenue), Madaripur Sadar, Madaripur. The plaintiffs knew nothing about the said case before that occasion. The order dated 28.02.1974 passed in the aforesaid case was obtained ex-parte in collusion with the process server showing the service of summon of Aziz Mollah being hanged. The deed of sale dated 03.04.1974 being No. 2679 fabricated by the defendant No. 1 is nothing but a mere paper transaction as A. Wahed Howlader had no saleable interest in the suit land. The order dated 06.01.2005 passed by the defendant No. 15 canceling the mutation of the plaintiffs is illegal, void and inoperative. Thus, the defendant No. 1 denied the title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land on the basis of his aforesaid created documents.

4. Hence, the plaintiffs were constrained to institute the suit.

5. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material averments made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit reveals no cause of action and it is bad for defect of parties and barred by limitation. The further case of the defendant No. 1, in short, is that A. Wahed Howlader mortgaged the suit land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. Accordingly, a deed of sale with a deed of re-conveyance got registered. A. Wahed Howlader requested Aziz Mollah to execute the return deed of sale after repayment of the consideration money but Aziz Mollah denied. Thereafter, A. Wahed Howlader filed Miscellaneous Case No. XIII- 3137/M-1005/1972-73 before the C.O (Revenue), Madaripur and Aziz Mollah contested the case by filing written objection. Ultimately, the said case was allowed on 28.02.1974 and Wahed Howlader took over possession of the suit land on 11.04.1974 and sold out the same by a registered deed of sale dated 03.04.1974 being No. 2679. Aziz Mollah instituted Title Suit No. 324 of 1974 before the 1a Court of Munsif Adalat, Madaripur and the said suit was dismissed. The defendant No. 1 has been enjoying the possession of the suit land by paying rents after getting his name mutated. The suit land was recorded in the present survey in the name of the defendant No. 1. Hence, the suit instituted by the plaintiffs is liable to be dismissed with cost.

6. The plaintiff’s side examined as many as 3 witnesses and on the other hand, the defendant side examined as many as 4 witnesses to prove their respective cases. The trial Court on perusal of the evidences on record and examination of the materials on record decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs.

7. The defendant No. 1 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment, and decree passed by the trial court preferred Title Appeal No. 36 of 2008 before the Court of District Judge, Madaripur who transferred, the some to the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Madaripur for hearing and disposal, the appellate court allowed the appeal upon reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the appellate court, the plaintiffs-petitioners preferred revisional application before this court and obtained the present rule.

9. At the time of hearing Mr. Mesbahul Islam (Asif), the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners. On the other hand, no one appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

10. Mr. Mesbahul Islam (Asif), the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal in accordance with the provisions as laid down under Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the learned Judge of the trial court rightly and properly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs with the findings that the suit is not barred by limitation as the defendant No. 1 fraudulently obtained the orders and deeds in question; that the deed of sale as well as deed of re- conveyance dated 11.02.1965 in question for 7 years expired on 11.02.1972 long before the promulgation of Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 dated 03.08.1972 under P.O. 44 of 1972 which is not applicable in the present suit; that A. Wahed Howlader had no saleable interest in the suit land after the said 11.02.1972 for which the deed dated 03.04.1974 being No. 2679 is inoperative and he had no possession of the suit land on 11.04.1974. The appellate court without adverting the aforesaid findings of the trial court improperly reversed the same and thereby committed an error of law which occasioned a failure of justice.

11. He further submits that the trial court after framing proper issues and on considering the evidence of both the parties rightly and properly decreed the suit assigning proper reasoning's but the appellate court without considering the correctness of reasoning's by which the trial court took decision in favour of the plaintiffs-petitioners improperly set-aside the same without assigning proper reasoning's thereof Thus, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court cannot be sustained in law.

12. He next submits that the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners had been able to prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence before the trial court but the defendant could not prove his case stating in the written statement by adducing oral and documentary evidence that he has any possession in the suit land. Thus, the trial court on considering the evidence of the respective parties and the facts and circumstances of the case and also the relevant provision of law rightly and properly decreed the suit of the plaintiff but the appellate court without proper perusal of the evidence on record and on misreading the evidence on record, misconstrued the fact and thereby arrived at a wrong decision by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court which occasioned a failure of justice. Thus, he prayed for set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court.

13. At the time of hearing, the learned Advocate for the petitioners filed a supplementary affidavit dated 21.05.2015 annexing the latest survey and submits that the B.S. record of right has been prepared in the name of the petitioners which reveals that the petitioners are in possession in the suit land.

14. Heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners and perused the revisional application along with the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court as well as the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and examined the papers annexed with the revisional application and also the exhibits. I have also perused the lower court records.

15. For proper disposal of the Rule, let as examine the trial court judgment at first. The trial court on considering the pleadings of the respective parties framed as many as 6 issues in the suit-

I) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form?

II) Whether the suit is barred by limitation?

III) Whether the suit is barred by defect of parties?

IV) Whether the plaintiffs have title and possession in the suit land?

V) Whether the Miscellaneous Case No. 1005/1972-73 dated 28.02.1974 and Miscellaneous Case No. 14/2003-2004 dated 06.01.2005 is illegal and in effective?

VI) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get relief as prayed for?

16. While deciding the issues, trial court examined 3 P.Ws and 4 D.Ws. The trial court at first discussed the issue No. 3 and found that though the defendant in his written statement stated that the suit is barred by defect of parties but he did not specifically mentioned the names of the respective persons and also at the time of cross-examination there is no such allegation made out by the defendant as such the trial court decided that the suit is not barred by defect of parties.

17. The trial court next discussed the issue No. 2 and found that the defendant side in their written statement stated that the grand-father of the plaintiff Abdul Aziz Mollah being aware of the Miscellaneous Case. Thus, the plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the suit after long laps of time but the plaintiff’s side claimed that they had no knowledge about the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case and the title suit mentioned by the defendant. The plaintiffs claim is that they Caine to know about the deed in question on 06.01.2005, when the defendant denied the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land.

18. The trial court considered the exhibit-6 and believed the evidence and the argument advanced by the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs that if the order dated 28.02.1979 was an illegal order and obtained by fraud then there is no question of limitation as claimed by the defendant. Thus, the suit is not barred by limitation.

19. The trial court, thereafter, decided issue Nos. 1, 4, 5 and 6 and found that admittedly Abdul Wahed Howlader was the original owner of the suit land and R.S. and S.A. Khatian was rightly prepared in their names exhibit-1 series. Abdul Wahed Howlader sold 0.50 acres of land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs Abdul Aziz on 01.02.1965 vide registered deed No. 673 exhibit-4 of the same date Abdul Aziz Molla executed and registered an Ekrarnama in favour of Abdul Wahed Howlader for 7 years exhibit-(Ka).

20. It is the case of the defendant that Abdul Wahed Howlader within the time limit asked to return the kabla but the predecessor of the plaintiff Abdul Aziz Molla refused.

21. The trial court found that there is no such evidence in support of the aforesaid claim on behalf of the defendant and after expiry of 7 years on 11.02.1972, the predecessor of the defendant failed to perform his duty to pay the consideration money and returned the same.

22. The trial court also considered the P.O. 49 of 1972 promulgated on 03.08.1972 and the provision of Section 95(Ka) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and also considered the decisions in the case of Bangladesh vs. Haji Abdul Gani Biswas and others report in 32 DLR(AD) 233 and found that the decision is applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present suit and deed No. 673 dated 11.02.1972 became out and out a sale deed and after the expiry of the aforesaid deed dated 11.02.1972, the predecessor of the alleged defendant had no right and title in the suit land and the subsequent order passed by the Revenue Officer vide CO. Revenue Officer Miscellaneous Case No. 1005/1972-73 is illegal and the subsequent deed on the basis of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case vide deed dated 03.04.1974 on the basis of the aforesaid Revenue Case is also illegal and ineffective and the defendant No. 1 has got no right, title and interest by the aforesaid deed.

23. The trial court also decided that as the deed dated 03.04.1974 is an ineffective deed and no right, title and interest accrued by the defendant and the deed dated 11.02.1972 is not M existence and the plaintiffs have right, title and interest by inheritance and the order of cancellation dated 06.01.2005 is also illegal which was passed improperly against the plaintiff.

24. The trial court then discussed about the possession in the suit land and found that the defendant No. I claimed that the deed is executed and registered on 03.04.1974 but it is claimed that Abdul Wahed Howlader obtained possession on 11.04.1974 through Court which is impossible and contradictory as the defendant No. 1 was not a party in the Miscellaneous Case. So, this contention of the defendant is not believable at all.

<u>25. On the aforesaid discussions trial court arrived at a decision that as the right, title and possession of the plaintiffs is established by the evidence, the plaintiffs are entitled to get relief as claimed and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs.</u>

<u>26. On its turn the appellate court while considering the claim of the defendant considered the exhibit-I and 1(Ka) and Exhibit-4 deed dated 11.02.1965 and also the Ekramama dated 11.02.1965 exhibit-(Ka).</u>

27. The appellate court also discussed the claim and counter claim of the respective parties. The appellate court also considered the certified copy of the order sheet of exhibit-Kha from which it appears that Abdul Wahed Howlader filed redemption case on 29.06.1973 under section 95(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The opposite party appeared on 26.11.1973 and prayed for time. On the next date on 06.12.1973 written statement was submitted on behalf of the opposite parties. Thereafter on 28.02.1972 redemption case was allowed. From exhibit-Kha-2, the appellate court found that Shahjahan Molla son of Abdul Aziz Molla filed a review case on 12.04.1974.

28. The appellate court also found the process server Abdul Latif went to the place of occurrence for execution of the possession to the decree-holder. The alleged deed was registered on 03.04.1974 in favour of the defendant No, 1 (exhibit-Gha). From the certified copy of the Miscellaneous Case (exhibit-Cha) and Title Suit No. 324 of 1974 filed by Abdul Aziz Molla on 02.12.1974 wherein Abdul Wahed Howlader was defendant and it was dismissed on 15.01.1975. The appellate court also considered the rent receipt filed by the defendant (exhibit-Chha series). The appellate court also considered the rent receipt filed by the plaintiff side, D.C.R. Exhibit-3 series. From where it appears that the plaintiff side paid Tk. 30/= for mutation on 24.07.2002 and paid rent for the year of 2003 and 2004. The appellate court also found that the predecessor of the plaintiff Abdul Aziz Molla or Shajahan Molla did not mutate their names and paid any rent more than 30 years to the Government

29. The appellate court also discussed the evidence of the P.Ws. 2 and 3 and found that they have deposed suppressing the facts. The appellate court also considered the evidence of the D. Ws. 1, 2, 3 and 4 and found that there is no contradiction in the evidence of the defendant witnesses. The appellate court also discussed about the redemption case which was allowed in favour of Abdul Wahed Howlader and the possession given to the predecessor of the defendant Abdul Wahed Howlader on 0904.1979.

30. On considering the aforesaid evidence, the appellate court found that the plaintiffs could not prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence. On the other hand, believed the evidence of the defendant side and also found that the defendant No. 1 purchased the land on 03.04.1974 before obtaining possession by the seller Abdul Wahed Howlader and thereafter, after registration of the deed, delivered the possession to the defendant No. 1. The appellate court also disbelieved the contention of the evidence of P.Ws. that Abdul Aziz Molla had no knowledge about the Miscellaneous Case and title suit. It was created by false personification.

31. The appellate court also disbelieved the full contention of the plaintiff witnesses and found that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land. The appellate court also considered the provision of Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the decision referred to by the plaintiff-appellant reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 and also considered the decision reported in 34 DLR 237 wherein transaction passed and closed principle was set-aside.

32. The appellate court found that on 11.04.1974, according to order in redemption case dated 28.02.1974, possession was given to Abdul Wahed Howlader before that i.e. on 03.04.1974 Abdul Wahed Howlader, sold the suit land to the defendant No. 1 and handed aver possession. On that time the principle of transaction passed and closed, was not established by the Court. It was published in the year of 1980 after obtaining possession by the defendant No. 1.

33. The appellate court also found that the plaintiff's side did not file the suit within 6 years from the aforesaid decision "Principle on transaction passed and closed" and did not file the suit within 12 years from the dispossession by the defendant. The plaintiff side failed to prove that they are possessing the land and so the suit is barred by limitation.

34. The appellate court further found that though the deed dated 11.02.1965 was within the purview of principle transaction passed and closed but the plaintiff being out of possession have lost their title in the suit land, and the appellate court with the aforesaid findings and observations set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court.

35. It appears from the judgment and decree passed by the courts below that the trial court framed proper issues in the suit and decided those issues on considering the evidence of both the parties and the relevant provision of law and fact and decreed the suit.

36. The appellate court reversed the same with the contention mainly that the suit is barred by limitation and the plaintiffs have no possession in the suit land. Though, the appellate court admitted that the alleged deed of the defendant No. 1 executed and registered on 03.04.1974 by Abdul Wahed Howlader but possession was given to him on 11.04.1974 from which it reveals that while he was not in possession i.e. the plaintiffs were in possession and if the plaintiffs were not in possession and there was no question of possession through process server on 11.04.1974 and before obtaining possession how he transferred the land on the same date i.e. 03.04.1974. The appellate court did not consider this factual aspect at all and believed that the defendant is in possession, is not a proper appreciation of the facts and circumstances of the case. The next point is that the appellate court found that the plaintiff did not file the suit within 6 years from the publication of the judgment by the appellate court after principle transaction passed and closed and also did not file the suit within 12 years of dispossession. This, findings is not also a proper finding's of fact.

37. The appellate court further found that the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not mutate their name and long after 30 years, the plaintiffs have mutated their names and paid rent to the Government.

<u>38. From the aforesaid contention it cannot be concluded that the right and title cannot be brushed aside by not mutating the name or names by the plaintiffs.</u>

39. On the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it appears that the appellate court wrongly held that the suit is barred by limitation and the plaintiffs have no possession in the suit land. It is evident from the evidence of the P.Ws that P.Ws. 2 and 3 corroborated the evidence of P.W. 1 that they are in possession in the suit land long before and they have paid rent to the Government and from the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioners, it appears that the B.S. record has prepared in the name of the plaintiffs.

40. From where, it is presumed that the plaintiffs are in possession in the suit land. It appears from the evidence on record that the defendant side produced some certified copies of the order of Revenue Officer and the subsequent orders but in support of their claim they could not prove by adducing proper evidence that those are genuine and passed in accordance with law. Rather, it reveals that it was obtained fraudulently by practicing fraud upon the Court. Thus, the existence of the aforesaid proceeding can be questioned at any time and there is no limitation in the facts and circumstances prevails in the suit before this Court. The reasoning's given by the appellate court of filing suit out of time is not proper and not based upon the fact and law relevant to the suit.

41. The learned Advocate for the petitioners also referred to some decisions in the case of Mahadeb Chandra Mondal and another vs. Dulal Chandra Mondal and other reported in 25 BLD (AD) 233 wherein it is held, "State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950-Section 95A-As the date of re-conveyance expired before the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 came into force, the transaction in question could not be treated as a usufructuary mortgage transaction and the appellant was no entitle to get back the case land on the basis of Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act."

<u>42. In the case of Abdus Salam Sheikh and others vs. Puspa Rani Shil and others reported in 16 BLD (AD) 299 wherein it is held, "State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950-Section 95A-The clear legislative intent of Section 95A is that cases of sale attended with agreement for re- conveyance whether registered or unregistered would come within the ambit of complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of 7 years and provisions of section 95(4) (5) would apply to such transfer. A contrary view would apply to such transfer. A contrary view would clearly make the provision of Section 95A nugatory and frustrate its purpose."</u>

43. And in the case of Bangladesh vs. Haji Abdul Gani Biswas and others reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 wherein it is held, "Transactions subsisting when P.O. 88/72 was promulgated are hit by Section 95A save and except those which were not alive when P.O. 88/72 was promulgated being transactions past and closed."

44. From the discussions made above and on considering of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the decision referred to by the learned advocate for the petitioners, I am of the view that the appellate court without considering the evidence on record and the relevant provision of law, arrived at a wrong decision and illegally set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and thereby committed an error of law which occasioned a failure of justice. Thus, the rule succeeds.

45. In the result, the rule is made absolute.

46. The judgment and decree dated 29.04.2012 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Madaripur in Title Appeal No. 36 of 2008 is hereby set-aside.

47. The judgment and decree dated 21.07.2008 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Madaripur Sadar, Madaripur in Title Suit No. 40 of 2005 is hereby restored. The suit is decreed.

48. The order of stay granted earlier by this court is vacated.

49. Send down the lower court records along with a copy of this judgment to the trial court at once.

End.
